transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-04-07 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jake Coleman (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Michael Chen (Head of ML, Starlight), Sara Gomez (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Customer evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a multilingual assistant and internal automation. Key concerns: context window (32k vs 64k), tool-calling/function-calling, latency vs cost tradeoffs, compliance (SOC2, KMS), and run benchmarks on customer prompts. Next steps agreed: Redwood to send perf/pricing matrix, customer to share prompts, schedule SE deep dive.

00:00 Jake: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jake from Redwood, I'm the AE on this one, with Priya our solutions engineer.
00:08 Michael: Hey Jake, thanks, appreciate it. We wanted to walk through model selection — like, which open models make sense for our workloads and what tradeoffs look like.
00:16 Priya: Great — quick agenda: 1) your requirements (context length, multilingual, tool calling), 2) model options (open models + Redwood variants), 3) hosting options and perf/cost, 4) next steps. Sound good?
00:24 Liam: Yep. Quick background: Starlight is building an internal assistant for customer ops and a separate customer-facing multilingual chat. We'll also need backend tool-calls to our order system and a synthesis pipeline that ingests long tickets — so context length is important.
00:38 Sara: Plus we have data residency constraints in EU for customer-facing chat.
00:42 Jake: Got it. When you say "context length is important", what distribution are you seeing — average ticket length and tails?
00:49 Michael: Average is maybe 1.5k tokens, but for escalations we see 30–40k tokens sometimes, those are long threads with attachments. We don't necessarily need full 40k for every inference but we need to preserve recent thread and some historical context.
01:05 Priya: Okay — so this drives a couple options: either use shorter context models with prefix/KV caching and selective condensation, or pick large-context models — e.g., Redwood's verified 32k and 64k open model builds. For multilingual, are you mainly European languages plus English?
01:22 Michael: Yes — EN, FR, DE, ES primarily; occasional Portuguese and NL. Latency matters for user-facing chat — target P95 < 1.2s for short queries, but for long-context summarization longer is fine as long as throughput is reasonable.
01:36 Jake: Quick callout on tool-calling — Redwood supports function/tool calling semantics (JSON outputs, structured tool calls). Priya, do you want to talk about how we route tool calls and security?
01:45 Priya: Sure. We support function calling surface at the API level and you can restrict which tools a model can call via policies. For Dedicated/Private we can configure network paths to your internal APIs (VPC peering or private link). Calls can be proxied through Redwood or executed by customer infra depending on your security posture.
02:00 Sara: That proxy vs. direct — if proxied through Redwood Hosted, does PII leave our VPC?
02:07 Priya: If you use Hosted API, payloads go through Redwood processing and customer data may be processed in our hosted environment; for stricter needs Dedicated or Private is recommended — Private keeps the runtime in your VPC or on-prem and keys never leave your KMS.
02:18 Liam: What about SOC2 and audit logs? We need full auditability for those customer interactions.
02:24 Jake: We have SOC2, and Dedicated/Private give you richer audit log retention and token-level traces in the Redwood Console. We'll share the security pack after the call.
02:34 Michael: Cool. Back to models — what open models should we consider? We've seen references to Llama 3, Mistral-Instruct, and some big open 70B models. We're also looking at cost — we want sub-$0.01 per 1k tokens ideally for high volume.
02:50 Priya: Broadly: Llama 3 variants (Redwood-curated builds) are good generalists and often cost-effective with quantization; Mistral family are strong on code and instruction-following in some workloads; Mistral 22B/30B are interesting for cost. For 32k+ windows you hit fewer options — some Llama 3 and specialized long-context forks support 32k and 64k. We also maintain Redwood-verified benchmarks with latency and cost profiles.
03:10 Michael: Are there quality regressions with quantized models? We saw some hallucination increase on a previous vendor's 4-bit runs.
03:16 Priya: Good question — quantization can impact certain tasks. We recommend evaluation across your prompt sets. Redwood's Optimize tooling suggests quantization level by workload and flags regressions in quality monitoring. For critical customer-facing generation we often keep higher precision or run a small ensemble check.
03:31 Sara: For multilingual, do the open models have parity across FR/DE/ES or do we need specialized models?
03:36 Priya: There's variance. Llama 3 does okay across major EU languages, but for more niche coverage or legal/regulatory language you may want to test multilingual-specific models or apply translation + reranking. We'll recommend a shortlist to test.
03:50 Liam: What about tool-calling with long context — does KV cache get preserved across calls or dropped?
03:56 Priya: The runtime manages KV cache per session; for Dedicated and Private we can tune cache sizes and eviction to preserve relevant context. There's also prefix caching and automatic condensation plugins that reduce token usage while keeping salient info. Note that for Hosted we have sane defaults; Dedicated gives more tunability for throughput/latency.
04:16 Michael: Latency targets — we said P95 <1.2s for short queries; what are realistic numbers on our side for 32k and 64k?
04:23 Priya: For a 32k-capable model on a typical GPU with Redwood's optimized runtime, short single-turn queries should be similar to 8k models within 200–300ms overhead; long-context generation will be higher — e.g., context prep may add 300–800ms depending on KV operations. For 64k you often pay an extra overhead, so cost and latency go up. We'll provide benchmark numbers on the spreadsheet.
04:45 Michael: That'll help. On the Hosted pricing — do you have per-token rates for different model classes?
04:50 Jake: Yes — we'll send a matrix. Quick note: Dedicated is commit-based with better unit economics at scale and Private is priced as enterprise license + infra.
04:59 Sara: We have an internal compliance question: KMS integration — does Redwood work with our Azure Key Vault or GCP KMS?
05:05 Priya: We integrate with common KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can integrate with customer-managed keys for some plans; we'll confirm specifics in the security pack.
05:16 Liam: Good. On open models, can we lock model versions and do rollouts? We want canarying when we change model versions for the customer-facing bot.
05:23 Jake: Absolutely — Redwood supports version pinning and rollout policies (canary/A-B) with automatic fallback to a stable variant if latency or quality regressions are detected. The Console gives route-level dashboards for that.
05:34 Michael: For evaluation I'd like to run three models on our prompts: a 32k Llama 3 variant, a Mistral 22B quantized for cost, and a 64k long-context variant if available. Can Redwood run those benchmarks in your infra or should we run locally?
05:48 Priya: We can run hosted benchmarks on Redwood's test cluster with your prompt set (redact PII) and provide latency/cost/quality metrics. For Private concerns we can also provide a benchmark config for you to run locally. Which do you prefer?
05:58 Michael: Let's start with Redwood-run tests so we can get apples-to-apples. We'll redact sensitive bits.
06:03 Jake: Great. I'll follow up with the benchmark sheet. A few practical notes: please include typical prompt frequency, burst patterns, and acceptable tail latencies. Also note any regulatory rules that would require on-prem.
06:14 Sara: We'll add that. One other thing — tool-calling security: can we restrict widget calls to only internal endpoints and disallow third-party connector access?
06:23 Priya: Yes — policy controls let you scope tools by route and model; in Dedicated/Private you can enforce network-level restrictions.
06:30 Liam: Any gotchas about model tokenization differences across languages — for example some languages costing more tokens than others?
06:36 Priya: Tokenization does vary; some languages or emoji heavy content can blow up token counts. Our Optimize toolkit gives per-language token estimates and suggests condensation or translation fallback to reduce cost.
06:48 Michael: Cool. Let's talk timeline — we're aiming for pilot Q3, with a production decision end of Q3. Security review and procurement in May/June. Is that workable?
06:58 Jake: Yes — that's reasonable. We'll prioritize getting the perf/pricing sheet this week and aim to schedule the SE deep dive for next week.
07:06 Sara: Any legal red flags early — DPAs, standard contract terms?
07:10 Jake: We have standard DPA and security docs; legal can engage after the security call.
07:15 Michael: Ok, a couple of smaller clarifying questions — do you support tool-call tracing in logs so our audit team can see which functions were invoked and with what inputs (redacted)?
07:24 Priya: Yes — dedicated logging for function calls and ability to redact or hash inputs for PII concerns. We'll detail retention policies in the pack.
07:33 Liam: For the demo, are there sample apps or templates for multilingual and long-session assistants?
07:37 Jake: Yes — we have quickstart templates and reference apps; we'll include links.
07:41 Michael: Awesome. Anything else from the Redwood side?
07:44 Priya: I'll note the initial benchmark config: 1) 32k Llama 3 variant, 2) Mistral 22B quantized, 3) 64k candidate; test set: 200 short chat turns, 50 long-thread summarizations, multilingual splits (EN/FR/DE/ES). We'll run latency/cost/quality and return CSV + summary.
08:06 Jake: Great. Quick recap and next steps — Jake to send perf/pricing matrix and links to security docs by Fri 2026-04-09; Michael to upload prompt sets by Sat 2026-04-10; Priya will propose benchmark runtime config and run preliminary hosted tests then share results. Schedule SE deep dive w/ infra team for week of 2026-04-13.
08:25 Michael: That sounds good. Thanks everyone.
08:28 Sara: Thanks, talk soon.
08:30 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: there are occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" instead of "KV cache"), some names may be slightly off. The transcript preserves filler words and overlaps.
